# Plan amendment: `PORT_MACOS_TO_WINDOWS_AMENDMENT_1.md`

> **Status**: This amends `specs/PORT_MACOS_TO_WINDOWS.md`. Read it after that doc.

> All citations now web-search-verified with the `EXA_API_KEY` enabled. Anything previously tagged `TODO(verify)` is either cleared below or remains an explicit `TODO(verify)`.

---

## A. `ort` version coexistence — RESOLVED

**Finding**: `ort 2.0.0-rc.12` declares both `directml` and `coreml` as features (`directml = ["ort-sys/directml"]`, `coreml = ["ort-sys/coreml"]`). Both RCs target the same ONNX Runtime 1.24 underneath.

**Implication**: we do NOT need two RCs. We can use `ort = "=2.0.0-rc.12"` (single version) in one workspace, gated per-target:

```toml
# oracle-core/Cargo.toml — single RC, single feature per target
[dependencies]
ort = { version = "=2.0.0-rc.12", default-features = false, features = ["std", "ndarray"] }

[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
ort = { version = "=2.0.0-rc.12", default-features = false, features = ["std", "ndarray", "coreml"] }

[target.'cfg(target_os = "windows")'.dependencies]
ort = { version = "=2.0.0-rc.12", default-features = false, features = ["std", "ndarray", "directml"] }
```

**Caveats (verified by cited sources)**:
- Cargo feature unification in workspaces can cause issues for target-conditional features. Mitigation: `default-features = false` + explicit per-target re-enables.
- Cargo issue #11779 (open): target-specific features don't always resolve in workspace deps. **Verify with `cargo metadata` in F1 milestone prep before committing the snippet.**

**Old plan to delete**: the F1 prep claimed "fix the Windows RC to rc.12, leave macOS on rc.10". Replace with: migrate everything to `=2.0.0-rc.12` with feature flags.

**Sources**:
- <https://docs.rs/crate/ort/latest/source/Cargo.toml>
- <https://docs.rs/crate/ort/latest/features>
- <https://github.com/pykeio/ort/blob/main/Cargo.toml>
- <https://github.com/pykeio/ort/discussions/588>
- <https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/features.html>
- <https://nickb.dev/blog/cargo-workspace-and-the-feature-unification-pitfall/>
- <https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/11779>

---

## B. srt-win security model — RESHAPES Milestone C

**Finding**: Anthropic's srt-win (the closest production Windows sandbox reference) uses a 4-component stack:

1. **Dedicated `srt-sandbox` local user account** — provisioned by the broker, every sandboxed child runs as that user.
2. **Two-hop launch via `CreateProcessWithLogonW`** — broker (real user) → runner (srt-sandbox user, builds lockdown) → child (srt-sandbox user + restricted token).
3. **Restricted token** via `CreateRestrictedToken` with `SidsToDisable = [BUILTIN\Administrators, ...]` (logon SID strip is the load-bearing step).
4. **Job Object** for lifecycle (kill-on-close, memory, CPU).
5. **WFP filters** keyed on `srt-sandbox`'s SID for network confinement (loopback-only by default).
6. **Filesystem ACLs** via `srt-win acl grant|stamp|restore|revoke` — `allowRead`, `allowWrite`, `denyRead`, `denyWrite`. `denyWrite` takes precedence over `allowWrite` (write is allow-only with explicit denies); `allowRead` takes precedence over `denyRead` (read is broad-allow with explicit denies).

**Implication for devboule** (which has its own `SandboxPolicy { readonly_root, writable_paths, net, rlimits }`):

| devboule policy field | srt-win equivalent |
|---|---|
| `readonly_root` (no writes) | `denyWrite` ACE on the path (file: `MODIFY` DENY; parent: `FILE_DELETE_CHILD` DENY) |
| `writable_paths` | `allowWrite` ACE on each path |
| `writable_paths` (read) | `allowRead` covers it implicitly (read is broad-default) |
| `net::None` | no WFP filter = full block, OR `deny network*` ACL on the proxy port range |
| `net::Loopback` | WFP loopback PERMIT filter (port range like `60080–60089`) |
| `net::Enabled` | no WFP filter = full network |
| `rlimits` | win32job ExtendedLimitInfo |

**What's actually new (changes the plan)**:

- **The plan's C1+C2 ("Job Object + Restricted Token") is INSUFFICIENT for honest `is_enforced() -> true`.**
- A Windows backend in devboule MUST include a filesystem-ACL layer (`srt-win`-style or `rappct` AppContainer or both) AND a network-egress layer (WFP filter or Job Object + `deny network*` ACL or AppContainer capability gating).
- **New milestone introduced: C0 — Filesystem ACL layer (the missing piece)**. Without C0, `readonly_root` isn't enforced on Windows. The macOS code is correct because Seatbelt's deny-by-default filesystem rule covers it; on Windows, Job Object + Restricted Token don't see file permissions the same way.

**New milestone structure for C**:

- **C1**: Job Object (kill-on-close + memory/CPU limits)
- **C2**: Restricted Token (`CreateRestrictedToken` with `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | 4` + logon SID strip)
- **C3 (NEW, formerly implied)**: Filesystem ACL layer — `allowWrite` on `policy.writable_paths`, `denyWrite` on `policy.readonly_root`, `allowRead`/`denyRead` follow devboule's policy structure. Use raw `windows` crate + the `grantWindowsAcl` pattern from srt-win.
- **C4 (NEW)**: Network-egress layer — WFP filter for `srt-sandbox`-style SID keying OR simpler: `deny network*` for `NetPolicy::None`, loopback PERMIT for `Loopback`, no filter for `Enabled`.
- **`is_enforced() -> true` on Windows is now gated on C1+C2+C3+C4.** Until C3 lands, the docstring for `is_enforced()` says explicitly that file-deny coverage is partial (Job Object + Restricted Token are not Seatbelt-equivalent on filesystem rules).

**Old plan text to delete**: Milestone C's claim that C1+C2 cover the policy.

**Finding**: schema confirmed at <https://schema.tauri.app/config/2>.

## B. srt-win security model — RESHAPES Milestone C

**Finding**: Anthropic's srt-win (the closest production Windows sandbox reference) uses a 4-component stack:

1. **Dedicated `srt-sandbox` local user account** — provisioned by the broker, every sandboxed child runs as that user.
2. **Two-hop launch via `CreateProcessWithLogonW`** — broker (real user) → runner (srt-sandbox user, builds lockdown) → child (srt-sandbox user + restricted token).
3. **Restricted token** via `CreateRestrictedToken` with `SidsToDisable = [BUILTIN\Administrators, ...]` (logon SID strip is the load-bearing step).
4. **Job Object** for lifecycle (kill-on-close, memory, CPU).
5. **WFP filters** keyed on `srt-sandbox`'s SID for network confinement (loopback-only by default).
6. **Filesystem ACLs** via `srt-win acl grant|stamp|restore|revoke` — `allowRead`, `allowWrite`, `denyRead`, `denyWrite`. `denyWrite` takes precedence over `allowWrite` (write is allow-only with explicit denies); `allowRead` takes precedence over `denyRead` (read is broad-allow with explicit denies).

**Implication for devboule** (which has its own `SandboxPolicy { readonly_root, writable_paths, net, rlimits }`):

| devboule policy field | srt-win equivalent |
|---|---|
| `readonly_root` (no writes) | `denyWrite` ACE on the path (file: `MODIFY` DENY; parent: `FILE_DELETE_CHILD` DENY) |
| `writable_paths` | `allowWrite` ACE on each path |
| `writable_paths` (read) | `allowRead` covers it implicitly (read is broad-default) |
| `net::None` | no WFP filter = full block, OR `deny network*` ACL on the proxy port range |
| `net::Loopback` | WFP loopback PERMIT filter (port range like `60080–60089`) |
| `net::Enabled` | no WFP filter = full network |
| `rlimits` | win32job ExtendedLimitInfo |

**What's actually new (changes the plan)**:

- **The plan's C1+C2 ("Job Object + Restricted Token") is INSUFFICIENT for honest `is_enforced() -> true`.**
- A Windows backend in devboule MUST include a filesystem-ACL layer (`srt-win`-style or `rappct` AppContainer or both) AND a network-egress layer (WFP filter or Job Object + `deny network*` ACL or AppContainer capability gating).
- **New milestone introduced: C0 — Filesystem ACL layer (the missing piece)**. Without C0, `readonly_root` isn't enforced on Windows. The macOS code is correct because Seatbelt's deny-by-default filesystem rule covers it; on Windows, Job Object + Restricted Token don't see file permissions the same way.

**New milestone structure for C**:

- **C1**: Job Object (kill-on-close + memory/CPU limits)
- **C2**: Restricted Token (`CreateRestrictedToken` with `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | 4` + logon SID strip)
- **C3 (NEW, formerly implied)**: Filesystem ACL layer — `allowWrite` on `policy.writable_paths`, `denyWrite` on `policy.readonly_root`, `allowRead`/`denyRead` follow devboule's policy structure. Use raw `windows` crate + the `grantWindowsAcl` pattern from srt-win.
- **C4 (NEW)**: Network-egress layer — WFP filter for `srt-sandbox`-style SID keying OR simpler: `deny network*` for `NetPolicy::None`, loopback PERMIT for `Loopback`, no filter for `Enabled`.
- **`is_enforced() -> true` on Windows is now gated on C1+C2+C3+C4.** Until C3 lands, the docstring for `is_enforced()` says explicitly that file-deny coverage is partial (Job Object + Restricted Token are not Seatbelt-equivalent on filesystem rules).

version = "0.1.0"
description = "Devboule — local agent orchestration dashboard"
edition = "2021"
license = "Apache-2.0"

# disables Cargo's auto-discovery of `src/main.rs` — without this entry the app binary

name = "devboule"
path = "src/main.rs"

# Tauri AppHandle) Claude spawns before each tool call; it bridges Patch/Exec tool calls
# through the .aspis-agents.json consent file-bridge into the app's consent UI. The body
# lives in the lib (`run_claude_consent_hook`) so it reuses the same file-lock +
# serializer; this bin is a thin shim. Declared explicitly so it builds alongside the
# default `devboule` GUI binary (src/main.rs).
[[bin]]
name = "claude_consent_hook"
path = "src/bin/claude_consent_hook.rs"

[features]
default = []

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "2", features = [] }
libc = "0.2" # process-group kill for the sandboxed `run` tool timeout (unix)
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"
tauri-plugin-notification = "2"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["preserve_order"] }
regex = "1"
chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
# keyring 3.x ships NO default features: with none enabled it silently falls back
# to the in-memory `mock` store, where `set_password` returns Ok but the secret is
# kept only inside that one `Entry` object — a freshly constructed `Entry::new`
# returns `NoEntry`. That made EVERY vault credential (Oracle LLM key, provider
# tokens, device keys) appear to save yet never persist (Bug B). Enable the
# platform-native OS keystores; keyring compiles only the one matching the build
# target, so listing both is the correct Windows+macOS setup.
keyring = { version = "3.6", features = ["windows-native", "apple-native"] }
open = "5.3"
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls-tls", "stream"] }

# HTTP generation reads `reqwest::Response::bytes_stream()` on the shared async client,
# and the buffered CLI path spawns + (on cancel) kills a child via `tokio::process`.
# tokio is ALREADY in the tree transitively (via tauri); listing it directly with this
# feature subset is purely additive feature unification — no new top-level crate.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["process", "io-util", "rt", "time", "sync", "macros"] }
thiserror = "2"
urlencoding = "2.1"
sha2 = "0.10"
hex = "0.4"
getrandom = "0.3"
futures-util = "0.3"
fs2 = "0.4"
x25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["static_secrets"] }
ed25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["rand_core"] }
rand_core = { version = "0.6", features = ["getrandom"] }
aes-gcm = "0.10"
hkdf = "0.12"
tar = "0.4"
zeroize = "1.8"
subtle = "2.6"
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4"] }
notify = "6"
sysinfo = { version = "0.33", default-features = false, features = ["system"] }
# App-hosted agent terminals (PTY). Cross-platform by design (ConPTY on Windows,
# openpty on unix/macOS), so the dependency is NOT cfg-gated — only the program/
# args choice at spawn time is. Same stack/crate as the studied terax-ai (Apache-2.0).
portable-pty = "0.9"
# ripgrep's gitignore engine. Polis' file scanner uses `ignore::gitignore::Gitignore`
# to honor `.gitignore` + a custom `.oracleignore` at the scan root (gitignore-style,
# nested), UNIFYING Polis' ignore policy with the Oracle indexer's. Only the matcher
# (`Gitignore`/`GitignoreBuilder`) is used — NOT the threaded `Walk`/`WalkBuilder` — so
# the existing hand-rolled DFS walk (symlink guard, MAX_FILES descent stop, cycle guard)
# is preserved. `default-features = false` drops the unused parallel-walk machinery.

# of the DETERMINISTIC SANDWICH): per-item AST extraction + finding grounding
# (`censor/extract.rs`). NOT OS-specific, so NOT cfg-gated. ABI DISCIPLINE: each
# grammar crate exposes a `LanguageFn` from `tree-sitter-language` (^0.1, the stable
# ABI bridge) that `.into()`s to `tree_sitter::Language`; the grammar's direct
# `tree-sitter` dep is only a DEV-dep, so the runtime ABI is mediated by
# `tree-sitter-language`, NOT by a pinned tree-sitter version in the grammar. This is
# why `tree-sitter-rust` 0.24.x (dev-dep `tree-sitter ^0.24`) and
# `tree-sitter-typescript` 0.23.x (dev-dep `^0.24`) both link cleanly against the
# single `tree-sitter` 0.25 runtime here — `cargo tree -i tree-sitter` must show ONE.
# Grammars wired: Rust, TS/JS (the TSX grammar — the broadest of the TS family: it
# parses TS, JS, JSX, TSX, which is what we need since `FileLang::Ts` does NOT carry
# the exact extension and item-extraction + identifier-collection don't require a
# dialect-precise parser), Python, Go, C/C++, HTML, and Kotlin. `tree-sitter-go`
# 0.25.x and `tree-sitter-cpp` 0.23.x both follow the same ABI pattern (normal dep
# `tree-sitter-language ^0.1`; `tree-sitter` only a DEV-dep, ^0.24 for cpp — exactly

# 0.25 runtime — `cargo tree -i tree-sitter` still shows ONE. The C++ grammar parses
# both C and C++ (a strict superset for our extraction/identifier-collection needs,
# which don't require a dialect-precise parser), so `FileLang::Cpp` covers `.c`/`.h`
# too.

# `tree-sitter >=0.21,<0.23`, which would pull a SECOND `tree-sitter` runtime and break
# the single-tree-sitter invariant; the `-ng` fork uses the modern
# `tree-sitter-language ^0.1` normal dep (`tree-sitter` DEV-only `^0.24`), so it links
# against the SAME 0.25 runtime — `cargo tree -i tree-sitter` stays ONE.
tree-sitter = "0.25"
tree-sitter-rust = "0.24"
tree-sitter-typescript = "0.23"
tree-sitter-python = "0.25"
tree-sitter-go = "0.25"
tree-sitter-cpp = "0.23"
tree-sitter-html = "0.23"
tree-sitter-kotlin-ng = "1.1"

# built on macOS/Linux.
[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]

webview2-com = "=0.38.2"

# `oracle-core/metal` is compile-error on non-macOS — only enable here.
# ORT CoreML cannot run the Qwen3 ONNX export; Metal via Candle is the GPU path.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
objc2 = "0.5"
objc2-foundation = { version = "0.2", features = ["NSString", "NSError"] }
# "block2" unlocks evaluatePolicy_localizedReason_reply (the async reply-block
# API used by backend/auth.rs verify_user).
objc2-local-authentication = { version = "0.2", features = ["LAContext", "LAError", "block2"] }
block2 = "0.5"
oracle-core = { path = "../oracle-core", features = ["metal"] }

# which don't require a dialect-precise parser), so `FileLang::Cpp` covers `.c`/`.h`
# too.
#
# `tree-sitter-html` 0.23.x follows the SAME ABI pattern (normal `tree-sitter-language
# ^0.1`; `tree-sitter` DEV-only `^0.24`), so it unifies on the single 0.25 runtime.

tree-sitter-typescript = "0.23"
tree-sitter-python = "0.25"
tree-sitter-go = "0.25"
